newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - NOV 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - NOV 5.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The reasons for last night's gunboat collision with passenger ship Samaina off the island of Samos in the eastern Aegean in which four crew are still missing, are unclear. The gunboat, which was taking part in the 'Parmenion' military exercises, sank in 15 minutes after it was hit by the 1,767 tonne Samaina.
--The situation in the main opposition party New Democracy is headed for chaos as the two opposing camps appear determined to have a final face-off.
--The final decisions on the government's economic policies are expected today when Prime Minister Costas Simitis meets with his economic team and the governor of the central bank.

--Concern within ruling party PASOK at the government's tough economic measures but no public expressions of discontent until Simitis formally announces who will bear the burden of convergence with Europe.
--Simitis says those responsible for last night's gunboat collision are guilty of criminal negligence and must be made an example of.
--The Supreme Court is expected to announce a preliminary investigation into irregularities in spending by state bodies and the public sector amounting to 12 billion drachmas.
--New Democracy leader Miltiades Evert is expected to receive a petition from 25 MPs urging him and his opponents to compromise and save the conservative opposition party from the morass.
--Four young men and 10 billion drachmas go down in the Aegean. The gunboat 'Kostakos' was conducting military exercises when it collided with the Samaina 500 metres off the northern coast of Samos.
--Today's meeting of New Democracy's Political Council will be crucial in whether there will be any dialogue between the party's opposing camps.

--The customs code discussed in Parliament last night offers provisions to settle outstanding debts to the state, drawing a response from opposition MPs that the government is rewarding those who dodge tariffs and duties.
--The national health system is to get 15 new hospitals and 2,463 beds by 1999.
--The second shipping incident in a week draws shock and fury. The collision of the gunboat and the Samaina, in conditions that were not adverse, is inexplicable.
